summary: Cost Model API (SCM) elevated p99 latency after staged rollout (Console breakdown + Optimize what-if)
description:
Issue summary
- After enabling the SCM Cost Model API integration for Console cost breakdown (and a subset of Optimize what-if traffic), Cost Model API p99 latency in prod increased and triggered downstream timeouts in Console for some tenants.

Impact
- Internal: Console cost breakdown endpoint degraded for a subset of requests when SCM calls exceeded client timeouts; Optimize scenario sweeps showed increased wall-clock time in prod canary.
- Customer-facing symptoms (via Support): intermittent slow loading of cost breakdown sections; occasional fallback behavior where Console showed partial/estimated values with a banner (or $0 in edge cases when downstream cache path returned empty).

Detection
- Grafana alert: cost-model-service p99 latency > 900ms for 10m (target p99 250ms).
- Error budget burn increased due to timeouts at Console backend when SCM exceeded 800ms.

When
- First alert: 2025-03-07 10:42 PT
- Peak: ~11:05–12:10 PT

Current status
- Mitigated by reducing traffic to SCM via rollout flag gating + increasing server-side caching + temporarily disabling the highest-cost explain payload path for Console tooltips.
- p99 back within target as of 2025-03-07 13:02 PT; monitoring continued through 2025-03-09.

Environment / scope
- cost-model-service prod; elevated p99 most pronounced in us-east where the initial tenant cohort had higher QPS.
- Secondary impact observed in eu-west after Console cohort expansion.

Dashboards (internal)
- Grafana: Cost Model API Overview (p50/p95/p99, RPS, error rate)
- Grafana: SCM Cache Metrics (hit rate, key cardinality, redis latency)
- Grafana: Console -> SCM dependency panel (client timeout rate, fallback rate)

Initial hypothesis
- Increased cache miss rate due to request key explosion from high-cardinality request fields (e.g., request_id, actor metadata, and version negotiation headers) leaking into cache key.
- Additional per-request overhead from model-catalog lookups not being memoized under peak traffic.
- A minority of requests were hitting the /explain path with large breakdown payloads (tooltips), increasing serialization time and response size.

Triage notes (what we checked)
1) Confirmed elevated p99 in cost-model-service independent of API gateway.
2) Compared p99 vs CPU utilization: CPU moderate (~55–65%), but GC time increased on instances handling most traffic.
3) Cache hit rate dropped from ~0.82 -> ~0.34 after cohort expansion.
4) Redis latency normal; issue was cache key cardinality (cache effectiveness), not store performance.
5) Query logs showed repeated calls to model-catalog resolver for identical (model_id, sku, quant_profile) tuples.

Mitigation applied
- 11:18 PT: Rolled back Console tenant cohort from 20% -> 5% via feature flag (Benji Okafor), prioritized highest-value tenants with known stable behavior.
- 11:31 PT: Hot config change: enabled request-level memoization within cost-model-service for model-catalog and pricing-table reads (TTL 60s).
- 11:44 PT: Disabled Console tooltip enrichment that called /explain for every table row; Console now calls /estimate only, and loads explain on-demand (per user expand) (Chloe Martin).
- 12:05 PT: Increased cost-model-service autoscaling aggressiveness (min replicas +2) to reduce tail latency while cache warmed.

Root cause (most likely)
- Cache-key construction unintentionally included version-negotiation and tracing headers (and in some paths request_id), causing cache fragmentation post-rollout.
- Combined with synchronous model-catalog lookups per request, this increased tail latency under bursty traffic.

Resolution
- Post-mitigation, p99 stabilized at ~210–260ms in us-east and ~230–290ms in eu-west.
- Console timeouts and fallback rate returned to baseline.

Follow-ups / action items
- [SRE] Add alert on cache key cardinality + sudden cache hit-rate drops (owner: Rafael Mendes).
- [Platform] Ensure cache keys are derived only from canonical SCM inputs; explicitly exclude request_id, actor, trace headers (owner: Jordan Lee).
- [Console] Keep /explain on-demand only; document guidance in integration how-to (owner: Jada Williams).
- [Platform] Add perf regression test covering p99 under cohort expansion and mixed estimate/explain traffic (owner: Ethan Park).

Notes
- This ticket is internal-support for operational triage and mitigation tracking. Engineering work items are tracked via GitHub PRs and related platform tickets.
